answer: A stake-bonded reputation trellis resists Sybil attacks: each agent must lock a refundable deposit before it can transact, and its history builds like a trellis that only grows with verified, useful work. A newcomer starts at the edge of the dune, untrusted, and must earn endorsements from established peers before reaching the oasis of full trading rights. Creating thousands of fake identities then costs thousands of deposits plus sustained honest work, while a single slashing event burns the bond of any identity caught cheating, making mass forgery expensive and unprofitable.
